events.title: Battle of Cannae
events.description: Hannibal's Carthaginian army decisively defeated a much larger Roman force at Cannae in southeastern Italy, using a double envelopment tactic that destroyed most of the Roman army. Traditionally dated to August 2, 216 BC.
events.significance: Considered one of the greatest tactical victories in military history, it is still studied in military academies as the model of encirclement and remains a defining moment of the Second Punic War.

events.title: First U.S. Census Begins
events.description: The first United States census began under the direction of Secretary of State Thomas Jefferson and U.S. marshals, as mandated by the Constitution. It counted a population of about 3.9 million people.
events.significance: It established the tradition of a decennial census used to apportion seats in the House of Representatives and provided the first detailed demographic snapshot of the new nation.

events.title: Hitler Becomes Führer Following Hindenburg's Death
events.description: Following the death of President Paul von Hindenburg, Adolf Hitler merged the offices of president and chancellor, declaring himself Führer and Reich Chancellor of Germany. The armed forces swore a personal oath of loyalty to him.
events.significance: This consolidated Hitler's absolute dictatorial power in Germany, removing the last institutional check on his rule and paving the way for World War II and the Holocaust.

events.title: Iraq Invades Kuwait
events.description: Iraqi forces under Saddam Hussein launched a full-scale invasion of Kuwait and occupied the country within days, citing oil disputes and debt claims.
events.significance: The invasion triggered UN sanctions and led to the U.S.-led coalition's Gulf War in 1991, reshaping Middle Eastern geopolitics and international responses to aggression in the post-Cold War era.

events.title: Death of Wild Bill Hickok
events.description: Legendary gunfighter and lawman James Butler 'Wild Bill' Hickok was shot and killed by Jack McCall while playing poker in Deadwood, Dakota Territory. He was holding black aces and eights, later known as the 'dead man's hand'.
events.significance: His death cemented his status as an iconic figure of the American Old West and contributed to enduring frontier folklore.
